reason: H0 does not directly fuzz serialization of attacker-controlled malformed UTF-8. Its only serializer call, htmlDocContentDumpOutput, operates on a document first produced by htmlCtxtReadMemory, so parser processing constrains the strings reaching serialization; it also provides no XML save-path target. S1 specifically changes malformed-UTF-8 handling in three entity/attribute serialization functions to emit U+FFFD instead of aborting, making arbitrary invalid byte sequences, truncation positions, document type, attribute context, and doc->encoding state material fuzz dimensions.
evidence: In fuzz/html.c, docBuffer is first passed to htmlCtxtReadMemory; htmlDocContentDumpOutput then receives only the resulting doc.
H0 never directly supplies fuzz bytes as text or attribute content to a constructed xmlDocPtr, nor does it invoke an XML save interface exercising xmlEscapeEntities or xmlBufAttrSerializeTxtContent.
xmlEncodeEntitiesInternal now handles xmlGetUTF8Char failure by setting val = 0xFFFD and advancing cur.
xmlEscapeEntities now handles malformed bytes within explicit in/inlen bounds by emitting a replacement character and advancing one byte.
xmlBufAttrSerializeTxtContent has distinct behavior depending on doc == NULL or doc->encoding == NULL and now replaces invalid UTF-8 instead of aborting.
recommended_action: Add a serializer-focused target that constructs XML and HTML documents/nodes from raw fuzz-controlled, NUL-terminated byte strings; places those bytes in text and attribute values; varies doc type, attribute context, doc->encoding, and malformed/truncated UTF-8 placement; and exercises public entity-encoding and XML save APIs that reach xmlEncodeEntitiesInternal, xmlEscapeEntities, and xmlBufAttrSerializeTxtContent.
